questions.question: What is the full form of UNICEF?

options.text: United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund
United Nations Information, Culture and Educational Forum
United Nations Cultural and Educational Fund

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund **

**Explanation:**

UNICEF was established on December 11, 1946, by the United Nations General Assembly.

Initially known as the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund, it was created to provide emergency food and healthcare to children and mothers in countries that were devastated by World War II.

**Mandate and Mission:**

 
• UNICEF's mandate has evolved over the years, and it currently focuses on addressing the needs of children and mothers in both emergency and development contexts.
 
• The mission is to ensure that every child has the right to survive, thrive, and fulfill their potential, regardless of nationality, ethnicity, or background.

**Key Areas of Focus:**

 
• Health and Nutrition: UNICEF works to improve access to essential healthcare services, promote vaccinations, and address malnutrition.
 
• Education: UNICEF supports education programs, including access to quality schooling and skill development opportunities.
 
• Child Protection: The organization works to protect children from violence, exploitation, and abuse.
 
• Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH): UNICEF promotes access to clean water, proper sanitation, and hygiene practices.
 
• Emergency Response: UNICEF plays a crucial role in providing immediate assistance during humanitarian crises, including natural disasters and conflicts.

**Funding and Structure:**

 
• UNICEF is funded by voluntary contributions from governments, private donors, businesses, and individuals.
 
• It operates in over 190 countries and territories through country programs and National Committees, which are independent fundraising organizations in various countries.

**Advocacy and Partnerships:**

 
• UNICEF advocates for policies and programs that benefit children and works in partnership with governments, non-governmental organizations, and other UN agencies to achieve its goals.
 
• The organization collaborates with a wide range of stakeholders to address the diverse needs of children globally.

**Awards and Recognition:**

UNICEF has received numerous awards and honors for its contributions to child welfare, including the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Hepatitis A is a disease caused by bacteria.

2. Malaria is a disease caused by protozoa.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Hepatitis A:**

__
 
• Hepatitis A is a **liver inflammation caused** by the **hepatitis A virus (HAV). *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The virus is typically **transmitted** when an uninfected individual **consumes food or water contaminated with an infected person's faeces.**
 
• The disease is l**inked to contaminated water or food, poor sanitation, and and poor personal hygiene**.

**Malaria:**

 
• Malaria is a **protozoan disease** caused by** Plasmodium parasites. ***Hence, statement 2 is** correct.*
 
• It is **transmitted** to humans by the **bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitos.**
 
• **P. falciparum** is the most **dangerous malaria parasite** and the most common on the African continent.
 
• **Outside of Sub-Saharan Africa, P. vivax** is the most common malaria parasite.
 
• The** earliest signs of malaria** are fever, headache, and chills. 
 
• It usually shows **10-15 days after the infective mosquito bite **and can be mild and difficult to identify.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2de43afd6a42725f7e569bc2e4410a75b00222a5e8d27ed6fa32f60a5d93324a.png]

questions.question: Pattadakal, a UNESCO world heritage site, is located on the banks of River ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaprabha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pattadakal,** a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is situated on the banks of the** Malaprabha River.**
 
• **It** provides evidence of the** wealth of Chalukyan architecture** from the **7th and 8th centuries.**
 
• It is renowned for its** intricately chiselled temples.**
 
• It comprises a collection of **10 significant temples,** each with a unique architectural style.
 
• The settlement was referred to as** "Perti gal"** by the **renowned geographer Ptolemy **(about 150 AD).
 
• It was even used as the **ceremonial centre** where** kings were crowned and commemorated**.
 
• The temple complex at Pattadakal features **Dravidian, Aryan, and a combination of the two architectural styles.**
 
• It is also the venue for the** Pattadakal Dance Festival **or **Chalukya Utsava **with performers from all over the world congregating here. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tungabhadra:**

 
 
• The majority of the Tungabhadra River's course is in the Indian state of **Karnataka**.
 
• It then passes through the border states of** Telangana and Andhra Pradesh** until coming together with the **Krishna River **next to Gundimalla village in the Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana.
 
• The river's water is renowned for being sweet and is regarded as the **sweetest water in the entire world.**
 
 
 
• **Ghataprabha:**
 
 
• The Ghataprabha River, a significant** right-bank tributary of the Krishna River**, travels** 283 kilometres** east of Chikksangam before joining the Krishna River.
 
 
 
• **Bhima:**
 
 
• The Bhima River often referred to as the** Chandrabhaga River,** is a significant river in both** South and Western India.**
 
• It travels through the states of** Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana **for **861 kilometers** before emptying into the Krishna River.

questions.question: What amount has the Government of India allocated for setting up the Green Hydrogen Mission Centre?
questions.solution:

• These Centres will focus on research, skill development, and knowledge dissemination while fostering collaboration between **government, industry, and academia.**

• Public and private entities, including research institutes and universities, are encouraged to submit proposals for the R&D scheme.

• The mission will also help reduce India's dependence on fossil fuel imports, positioning the country as a global leader in green hydrogen technology.

questions.question: Who was recently appointed as the third Director General of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) during the 7th ISA Assembly in New Delhi?
questions.solution:

• **Ashish Khanna has been elected as the new Director General of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) during its 7th Assembly session, succeeding Ajay Mathur, whose term ends in March 2025.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• The Director General's responsibilities include assisting the Assembly in executing the ISA's mandate and supporting member countries in addressing common challenges related to solar energy deployment.

questions.question: The term 'dribble' is used in which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basketball.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The term** 'dribble'** is used in **Basketball.**
 
• In basketball, dribbling is bouncing the ball on the floor continuously with one hand at a time.
 
• It is the only legal way that a player may maintain possession of the ball while walking or running.
 
• The dribble allows for much faster advancement and thus more opportunities for scoring.
 
• It also provides an opportunity for a crafty player on the opposing team to "steal" the ball in mid-bounce.
 
• Dribbling **should be done with finger pads** and the fingers should be relaxed and spread.
 
• The wrist should be pushing the basketball, and the forearm should be moving up and down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Basketball is a team sport in which there are two teams of five players each.
 
• Players advance the ball by bouncing it while walking or running (dribbling) or by passing it to a teammate.
 
• On offense, players may use a variety of shots – **the layup, the jump shot, or a dunk; on defense.**
 
• They may steal the ball from a dribbler,** intercept passes, or block shots; either offense or defense **may collect a rebound.
 
• It is a violation to lift or drag one's pivot foot without dribbling the ball, to carry it, or to hold the ball with both hands and then resume dribbling.

options.text: It will survey 1.2 million coastal households and collect data on local fishing practices and equipment usage.
It will cover 1.2 million households in coastal areas and gather information on their income and employment in the fisheries sector.
It will cover 1.2 million households along India’s coastline and collect data on household sizes and socio-economic status.
It will track 1.2 million households along the coastline and focus on collecting data on fish stock and habitat health.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It will cover 1.2 million coastal households and gather data on socio-economic status and household sizes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The marine fisheries census will cover 1.2 million households along India’s coastline.
 
• Data on household sizes, socio-economic status, and fisherfolk engagement will be collected.
 
• The initiative aims to enhance India’s blue economy and provide insights for better policy making.
 
• Union Minister for Fisheries Rajiv Ranjan Singh emphasized the importance of such data in transforming the fisheries sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The census was launched on World Fisheries Day, marking its significance in supporting sustainable fisheries practices.
 
• The data collected will guide interventions aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of coastal fisherfolk.
 
• Alongside the census, the Centre also launched multiple projects to support marine and inland aquaculture sectors.
 
• The census plays a crucial role in shaping targeted policies to improve livelihoods and strengthen the fisheries sector in India.

questions.question: When is the Martyr's Day observed in India every year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__30 January__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Martyrs' Day is observed on **30th January to mark the death anniversary of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, popularly known as Mahatma Gandhi ji**.
 
• It also marks the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi in **1948 by Nathuram Godse**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Martyrs' Day, also known as Sarvodaya Day, is celebrated on various days like 30 January, 23 March, 19 May, 21 October, 17 November, and 19th November to honor the people who have sacrificed their lives for the nation.
 
• January 30 is observed as Martyrs Day nationally. On this day in 1948, Gandhiji was assassinated by Nathuram Godse. 23 March is the death anniversary of Bhagat, Sukhdev, and Rajguru, 19 May is celebrated as 'Language Martyrs Day', 21 October is celebrated as 'Police Martyrs' Day' (Police Commemoration Day),17 November is the death anniversary of Lal Lajpat Rai, and 19 November is the birthday of Rani Lakshmibai.

questions.question: What is the common name of the compound CaOCl₂?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bleaching powder.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It has a strong smell of chlorine.
 
• Uses:
 
 
• Used in bleaching clothes in the laundry
 
• Used in bleaching of cotton and linen in textile industries.
 
• Used as an oxidizing agent.
 
• used as a disinfectant for disinfecting water.
 
• Used as a bathroom cleaner
 
 
 
• Preparation-

 Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → CaOCl2 + H2O

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Washing soda** is Hydrated Sodium carbonate.

 
 
• Its chemical name is sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O).
 
• It is used in glass, soap, and paper industries.
 
 
 
• Plaster of Paris (POP), quick-setting gypsum plaster consisting of a fine white powder (calcium sulfate hemihydrate), which hardens when moistened and allowed to dry.
 
 
• It is also known as the Plaster of Paris because for the preparation of POP, the abundant gypsum was first found near the capital city of France i.e. Paris.
 
• The chemical formula of the Plaster of Paris is (CaSO₄)₂. H₂O.
 
 
 
• Slaked lime is chemically known as Calcium hydroxide.
 
 
• Slaked lime is obtained by the action of water on calcium oxide.
 
• When it is mixed with water, a small proportion of it dissolves, forming a solution known as limewater, the rest remaining as a suspension called milk of lime.

questions.question: Which country honoured Prime Minister Modi with its 'Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger' award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​Nigeria

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• 
 
**Prime Minister Narendra Modi** will be awarded the **Grand Commander of The Order of the Niger (GCON)** by **Nigeria**, making him the second foreign dignitary to receive this honor. The only previous foreign recipient was **Queen Elizabeth II** in 1969.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• This marks **Modi's 17th international award** conferred by a country, highlighting his role in strengthening India's global diplomatic ties.
 
• Modi arrived in **Nigeria** on the first leg of his **three-nation tour**, which also includes **Brazil** and **Guyana**, from **November 17 to 21, 2024**. His visit aims to enhance **India-Nigeria strategic ties**, with a focus on **democracy, pluralism**, and bilateral cooperation.
 
• India and Nigeria have shared a **strategic partnership since 2007**, with growing collaboration in sectors like **economic development, energy, and defense**. Over **200 Indian companies** have invested more than **USD 27 billion** in Nigeria.
 
• The visit also marks the **first Indian Prime Minister visit to Nigeria in 17 years**, underscoring the significance of the bilateral relationship.

questions.question: In which state is the Sarhul festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Sarhul is a popular festival celebrated by **various tribes in the Jharkhand region.** The festival is the tribal New Year and is celebrated by the Munda, Oraon, Ho, etc. tribes of Jharkhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• One of the most popular tribal festivals celebrated across the Jharkhand region, the Sarhul festival marks the beginning of New Year.
 
 
• It is celebrated by the Oraon, the Munda, and the Ho tribes, of the Jharkhand region.
 
• Celebrated every year in the first month of the Hindu calendar, on the third day of the moon or the fortnight of 'Chaitra', Sarhul marks the advent of the spring season or “Phaagun” and is celebrated till the month of June or “Jeth”.
 
• Sarhul means worship of trees. **Being close to nature, these tribes start the Sarhul festival with the worship of trees and other elements of nature.**
